item.content:encoded:
Residents of Stage One in Cunningham, opposite the Cunningham Community Post, are living in fear and feeling unsafe in their own neighbourhood after repeated thefts and robberies in the area.

A resident, who wishes to remain anonymous told fijivillage News that her home has been broken into three times, and she now avoids carrying her phone, handbag or money whenever she leaves the house because she fears being robbed.

She says she spends most of the day inside her home with the doors locked until her son returns from work, speaking to neighbours through the window because she is too afraid to go outside.

Insert: Resident on theft issue, 14th Aug 26

Residents claim homes have been broken into repeatedly, vehicles parked along the roadside have been targeted and crops, including cassava, have been stolen from plantations.

Another family reported household items, including a refrigerator, mattress, television stand and solar equipment, were stolen.

Residents also claim people have been robbed while walking along the road, with the robbers allegedly using nearby roads to escape.

They say many of the incidents have been reported to Police, but they are frustrated because they feel there has been little follow-up after the initial reports.

Another resident says thieves entered her home while the family was away and on another occasion while they were sleeping.

She says the repeated thefts forced her to close the family's canteen after business items were stolen.

Residents are now calling on the Government and the Fiji Police Force to increase patrols, particularly at night, and install more streetlights, saying poorly lit roads make it easier for criminals to operate.

An officer at the Cunningham Community Post told fijivillage News that the post is a community-based police facility and is responsible for receiving reports from residents before referring criminal matters to the larger police stations.

The officer says serious criminal cases are referred to the Valelevu and Nabua Police Stations, which are responsible for carrying out investigations.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says officers are expected to take the initial reports and make referrals to the larger police stations.

He says Cunningham is supported by patrols from the Valelevu and Nabua Police Stations.

ACP Vusonilawe says the concerns raised by residents regarding patrols will also be looked into.

He is also urging anyone with complaints about police conduct to contact the Police complaints line on 1681.

item.title: Littering fine to increase from $40 to $200 from September 1st
item.description: People caught littering in the country will face a $200 fine from 1st September, following Cabinet’s approval of changes to the litter regulations. This will increase from the current $40 penalty.
item.content:encoded:
People caught littering in the country will face a $200 fine from 1st September, following Cabinet’s approval of changes to the litter regulations.

This will increase from the current $40 penalty.

The government says the changes are aimed at strengthening action against littering across the country.

It says the changes will address problems with how litter laws are currently enforced and increase the outdated penalties.

The new regulations will also make it easier for Litter Prevention Officers, municipal councils and other authorised officers to enforce litter laws consistently.

Enforcement officers will receive training, while the process for issuing and paying fines will also be improved.

People will be able to pay their fines through digital payment options.

The government says it will increase public awareness about littering and the new penalties.

The new regulations will come into effect on 1st September 2026, following preparations by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change and other enforcement agencies.

item.title: Glitz and glamour as 70th FMF Hibiscus Festival launches in Suva
item.description: It was a night of glitz and glamour as the 70th Anniversary of the FMF Hibiscus Festival was launched last night at the Civic Centre where the Queen contestants took centre stage with their sponsors. Hibiscus Festival Director, Ellen Whippy-Knight says it was a media launch of the partnership between the contestants and their sponsors.
item.content:encoded:
It was a night of glitz and glamour as the 70th Anniversary of the FMF Hibiscus Festival was launched last night at the Civic Centre where the Queen contestants took centre stage with their sponsors.

Hibiscus Festival Director, Ellen Whippy-Knight says it was a media launch of the partnership between the contestants and their sponsors.

Whippy-Knight says it is a concept they created last year where the sponsor actually comes up and presents their contestant and vice versa.

She says it was also a very entertaining and a wonderful opportunity to see how the contestants have progressed from the weeks of training prior to this.

The Festival Director says taking the Hibiscus Festival back to Albert Park has been something that everybody in Suva has been looking forward to.

Insert: Whippy-Knight on contestants Aug 13

The Hibiscus Festival will start on 29th August at Albert Park in Suva.
